dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3201.text: Dry provisions, 𩝍. Formed from 食, with 非 indicating the sound. Between Chen and Chu, visiting one another to eat cooked wheat is called 餥.

shuowen:3202.text: Wine and food. Formed from 食, with 喜 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “With it one can steam grain and prepare wine and food.”

shuowen:3203.text: To provide food. Formed from 食, with 算 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3204.text: To provide sustenance. Formed from 食, with 羊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3205.text: To eat. Formed from 食, with 反 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3206.text: Mixed rice. Formed from 食, with 丑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3207.text: Provisions. From 人 and 食.

shuowen:3208.text: To pour soup over rice. Formed from 食, with 贊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3209.text: A midday meal. Formed from 食, with 象 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3210.text: An afternoon or evening meal, 餔. From 夕 and 食.

shuowen:3211.text: To eat when the day reaches the shen hour. Formed from 食, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3212.text: To swallow. Formed from 食, with 𣦼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3213.text: To eat a little. Formed from 食, with 兼 indicating the sound. Read like 溓溓 in “the wind 溓溓.” Another explanation: incorruptible and pure.

shuowen:3214.text: To bring food to the fields. Formed from 食, with 盍 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Bring food to those southern fields.”

shuowen:3215.text: The Zhou call bringing food 餉 by the word 饟. Formed from 食, with 襄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3216.text: To bring food, 饟. Formed from 食, with 向 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3217.text: To bring food. Formed from 食, with 貴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3218.text: People of a district drinking wine together. Formed from 食 and 鄉, with 鄉 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:3219.text: The appearance of a serving vessel filled full. Formed from 食, with 蒙 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Full is the bowl of food.”

shuowen:3220.text: People of Chu call visiting one another to eat wheat 飵. Formed from 食, with 乍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3221.text: To visit one another and eat wheat. Formed from 食, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3222.text: People of Qin call visiting one another and eating wheat 䭡䭓. Formed from 食, with 㥯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3223.text: The visiting and wheat-eating called 䭡䭓. Formed from 食, with 豈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3224.text: To depend on others for food. Formed from 食, with 胡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3225.text: The fragrance of food. Formed from 食, with 必 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Fragrant is its aroma.”

shuowen:3226.text: To feast. Formed from 食, with 芺 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The feasting with wine.”

shuowen:3227.text: Satiated. Formed from 食, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3228.text: Satiated. Formed from 食, with 肙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3229.text: Full or well fed. Formed from 食, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3230.text: Abundance or surplus. Formed from 食, with 余 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3231.text: The smell of spoiled food. Formed from 食, with 艾 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “餀 is called 喙.”

shuowen:3232.text: To send someone off. Formed from 食, with 戔 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Xianfu gave him a farewell feast.”

shuowen:3233.text: Providing food in the open country is called 餫. Formed from 食, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3234.text: A guest lodging. Formed from 食, with 官 indicating the sound. The Rites of Zhou: every fifty li there is a market, with a guesthouse and provisions to receive visitors coming for court audiences and diplomatic calls.

shuowen:3235.text: Greedy. Formed from 食, with 號 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3236.text: Greedy. Formed from 食, with abbreviated 殄 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Called 饕飻.”

shuowen:3237.text: Rice spoiled by heat. Formed from 食, with 歲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3238.text: Rice spoiled by dampness. Formed from 食, with 壹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3239.text: Rice gone sour or spoiled. Formed from 食, with 曷 indicating the sound. The Analects says: “Food damp-spoiled and sour.”

shuowen:3240.text: When grain fails to ripen, this is 饑. Formed from 食, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3241.text: When vegetables fail to ripen, this is 饉. Formed from 食, with 堇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3242.text: Hunger. Formed from 食, with 戹 indicating the sound. Read like the Chu expression for being angry with someone.

shuowen:3243.text: Hunger. Formed from 食, with 委 indicating the sound. Another explanation: spoiled fish is called 餧.

shuowen:3244.text: Hunger. Formed from 食, with 几 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3245.text: Hunger. Formed from 食, with 我 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3246.text: People of Wu call sacrificing 餽. Formed from 食 and 鬼, with 鬼 also indicating the sound.

shuowen:3247.text: A sacrificial libation. Formed from 食, with 叕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3248.text: A small libation offering. Formed from 食, with 兌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3249.text: When a horse eats much grain, its qi flows down on all sides. Formed from 食, with 夌 indicating the sound. [The physiological description is uncertain.]

shuowen:3250.text: To feed grain to a horse. Formed from 食, with 末 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3251.text: What remains after eating. Formed from 食, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3252.text: A kind of cake. Formed from 食, with 羔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3253.text: Three joining together. From 入 and 一, depicting the union of three. All graphs in the 亼 group contain 亼. Read like 集.

shuowen:3254.text: To close the mouth. From 亼 and 口.

shuowen:3255.text: All. From 亼, 吅 and 从. The Book of Yu says: “All said, Boyi.”

shuowen:3256.text: Thought. From 亼 and 冊.

shuowen:3257.text: This time, now. From 亼 and 乁; 乁 is the ancient form of 及.

shuowen:3258.text: A dwelling in a market is called 舍. From 亼 and 屮, depicting a house; 口 depicts its built foundation.

shuowen:3259.text: To join. From 亼 and abbreviated 曾; 曾 means to increase. All graphs in the 會 group contain 會.

shuowen:3260.text: To increase. Formed from 會, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3261.text: The sun and moon sharing a lodge and following the celestial station. Formed from 會 and 辰, with 辰 also indicating the sound. [The clause 合宿从辰 is uncertain.]

shuowen:3262.text: A storehouse for grain. Grain is hastily taken and stored, hence called 倉. From abbreviated 食; 口 depicts the granary's shape. All graphs in the 倉 group contain 倉.

shuowen:3263.text: The sound of birds and beasts coming to eat. Formed from 倉, with 爿 indicating the sound. The Book of Yu says: “Birds and beasts come together noisily.”

shuowen:3264.text: To enter. It depicts going down together from above. All graphs in the 入 group contain 入.

shuowen:3265.text: To enter. From 口, entering from outside.

shuowen:3266.text: To enter deeply into a mountain. From 山 and 入. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:3267.text: To buy grain. From 入 and 䊮.

shuowen:3268.text: Whole or complete. From 入 and 工.

shuowen:3269.text: Two 入. 兩 is formed from this. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:3270.text: An earthenware vessel for holding wine and other liquid. People of Qin beat it to mark the rhythm of songs. A pictograph. All graphs in the 缶 group contain 缶. [The word 𤖅 in the liquid description is uncertain.]

shuowen:3271.text: An unfired earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with 𣪊 indicating the sound. Read like 莩 in 筩莩. [The recorded pronunciation phrase is unusual.]

shuowen:3272.text: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with abbreviated 包 indicating the sound. Anciently Kunwu made pottery. Note: the Scribe's Primer pronounces it the same as 缶.

shuowen:3273.text: A jar. Formed from 缶, with 賏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3274.text: A jar with a small mouth. Formed from 缶, with 𠂹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3275.text: A small earthenware jar. Formed from 缶, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3276.text: A water-drawing jar, 𦉥. Formed from 缶, with 幷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3277.text: A jar for drawing water. Formed from 缶, with 雝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3278.text: An earthenware vessel flat underneath. Formed from 缶, with 乏 indicating the sound. Read like 𦐇.

shuowen:3279.text: A long-necked jar kept in readiness for fire. Formed from 缶, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3280.text: An earthenware object. Formed from 缶, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3281.text: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with 或 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3282.text: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with 薦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3283.text: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with 肉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3284.text: An earthenware vessel. Formed from 缶, with 霝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3285.text: A chip or defect. Formed from 缶, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3286.text: A vessel broken. Formed from 缶, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3287.text: A crack. Formed from 缶, with 虖 indicating the sound. Earthenware vessels readily crack in firing.

shuowen:3288.text: A vessel empty inside. Formed from 缶, with 殸 indicating the sound. 殸 is the ancient form of 磬. The Odes says: “The jar is empty.”

shuowen:3289.text: A vessel's contents exhausted. Formed from 缶, with 𣪠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3290.text: A vessel for receiving money. Formed from 缶, with 后 indicating the sound. Anciently made of earthenware; now of bamboo.

shuowen:3291.text: A vessel. Formed from 缶, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3292.text: Arrows for bows and crossbows. From 入, depicting the point, nock and feathers. Anciently Yimou first made arrows. All graphs in the 矢 group contain 矢.

shuowen:3293.text: A bow or crossbow discharging from near the body and hitting at a distance. From 矢 and 身.

shuowen:3294.text: A clamp for bending and straightening arrows. Formed from 矢, with 喬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3295.text: An arrow for shooting birds with a cord. Formed from 矢, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3296.text: The target shot at in the spring banquet. From 人 and 厂, depicting stretched cloth, with 矢 below. The Son of Heaven shoots bear, tiger and leopard targets, subduing ferocity; lords shoot bear, pig and tiger; grandees shoot deer, 麋 suggesting confusion; scholars shoot deer and pig, removing harm from the fields. The invocation says: “Do not be like an unruly lord who will not attend the king's court; therefore we oppose and shoot you.”

shuowen:3297.text: To injure. Formed from 矢, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3298.text: Things have length and shortness, with an arrow as the standard. Formed from 矢, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3299.text: “How much more”: a particle. Formed from 矢, with abbreviated 引 indicating the sound. 矢 is used because words travel toward their object like an arrow.

shuowen:3300.text: A word or utterance. From 口 and 矢.
